articles.title: Chill in some idle games with the new Fanatical Idler Bundle
articles.summary: Idle and clicker games have exploded in popularity over the last year - so here's your chance to experience some for cheaps. Fanatical's new Idler Bundle has some interesting looking selections for you.

articles.title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
articles.summary: I covered this topic live with Shishir Tewari, Senior Manager, Data Engineering at Procore, during GitHub Universe 2026. Our session was titled “Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills” .

articles.title: Life On Mars 2 – Pre Orders
articles.summary: Kai Magazine has just opened pre-orders on the sequel to their game Life On Mars. It's only being offered as a physical edition that includes an "audio enhancement chip", which can be heard in the intro above.

articles.title: Hacking Meta’s Smart Glasses
articles.summary: Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses have attracted plenty of controversy in the relatively short time they have been available, given their potential for covert and unvanted surveillance.

articles.title: 9to5Mac Daily: November 12, 2026 – OLED iPad Air rumors, MacBook Pro teardown
articles.summary: Listen to a recap of the top stories of the day from 9to5Mac . 9to5Mac Daily is available on iTunes and Apple’s Podcasts app , Stitcher , TuneIn , Google Play , or through our dedicated RSS feed for Overcast and other podcast players.

articles.title: Google rolling out Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 for Pixel
articles.summary: Report issues via the Android Beta Feedback app on Pixel devices. Access it from the application drawer or Quick Settings to file bugs in Google’s issue tracker.

articles.title: NVIDIA announce Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO following scandal
articles.summary: Oh my, Jensen Huang you very naughty boy. NVIDIA just announced that Huang has resigned as CEO following a recent scandal. Read the full article on GamingOnLinux .

articles.title: Claude Meetings lets Anthropic's AI join your video calls
articles.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings, a feature that puts Claude into video calls as a visible participant. During a call, Claude can answer questions, generate documents and whiteboards, and log notes and action items, responding in text by default and accessing connected tools when granted permission.

articles.title: Claude Code v2.1.323
articles.summary: Added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools; see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode to turn it on, or to turn it off for an organization.

articles.title: Opera One for iOS adds Data Saver feature, cutting browsing data usage by up to 80%
articles.summary: In today’s announcement, Opera also touted the arrival of Data Saver on Opera One for iOS, which the company says can reduce browsing data usage by up to 80% by compressing images and text on its servers before they reach the user’s device.

articles.title: With formidable female protagonists, check out the Green Man Gaming's Girls Just Wanna Have Guns! Bundle
articles.summary: Every purchase also supports Safe in Our World and its work raising mental health awareness across the games industry and beyond. The bundle also includes instant Steam key fulfilment and a bonus 3% voucher for a future Green Man Gaming purchase.

articles.title: Announcing Rust 1.100.0
articles.summary: The Rust team is happy to announce a new version of Rust, 1.100.0. Rust is a programming language empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient software.

articles.title: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen outscores the bigger Argon just four weeks after its launch
articles.summary: Unlike the frontier models Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon , which Google designed for deep, long-horizon reasoning on hard problems, Hydrogen is meant to handle everyday tasks quickly and cheaply.

articles.title: iOS 27’s Find My app adds convenient feature I’ve long wished for
articles.summary: iOS 27 is packed with new features, including several for the Find My app . One upgrade to Find My—custom sharing durations—grants a feature request I’ve had for years.

articles.title: Humble Bundle goes through a re-design that's being accused of messy vibe-coding
articles.summary: Fixing what isn't broken huh? Humble Bundle just completely remade their website and store, and lots of people are unhappy with it. It's full of issues, with many across social media (and my inbox - oh my) accusing them of forcing out a clearly not ready "vibe-coded" new store design.

articles.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
articles.summary: Jensen Huang’s resignation raises questions about Nvidia’s commitment to open source AI, including its Hugging Face acquisition, open-weight models, and advocacy against restrictions, as the company navigates a leadership transition.

articles.title: Apple Notes adds a powerful new advantage in iOS 27.3
articles.summary: There’s no shortage of note-taking apps on the App Store, but Apple Notes has long been my favorite, and in iOS 27.3 it’s gaining a new advantage: extensive app controls via Siri AI.

articles.title: Deals: Galaxy SmartTag 3 up to 30% off, Chromebooks, Google Home Speaker, Walmart early Black Friday now live, more
articles.summary: Today, Woot is offering the first chance to save on the brand new Samsung Galaxy SmartTag 3 . While the all-new Google Pixel Tag has arrived at the same $30 regular price , Woot is now offering as much as 30% off multi-pack bundles of the new Samsung tracker.

articles.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
articles.summary: We are bringing Gemini 4 Hydrogen to Google Search globally to provide you with more intuitive, visual, and precise answers. This update helps you navigate complex questions by understanding your intent, conducting simultaneous queries, and displaying structured information like tables and images.

articles.title: Kubernetes Python client gets a modern overhaul for the AI/ML era
articles.summary: Yet for the past several years, this critical bridge between Python and Kubernetes has operated in low-maintenance mode. As AI/ML workloads have exploded in scale and complexity, the gap between what modern AI infrastructure demands and what the legacy Python client was built to deliver has become impossible to ignore.

articles.title: Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open source AI after Jensen Huang’s exit
articles.summary: Huang’s advocacy for open source and open-weight AI has long extended beyond Hugging Face. In July, the CEO published an AI policy letter as his first-ever post on the social network X .

articles.title: Actions for ARM32 Linux & Windows retirement
articles.summary: GitHub Actions hosted runners will be ending support for ARM32 job execution on Windows and Linux by 8th Dec 2026. This follows our end of support for node20 where Node 24 does not support ARM32.

articles.title: ‘Hey Gemini’ hotword debuts on Android XR glasses
articles.summary: Around a decade after “Hey Google” made its debut, Google is introducing its first new always-listening hotword. “Hey Gemini” makes its debut on Google’s Intelligent Eyewear glasses powered by Android XR, with wearers able to use that hotword in place of “Hey Google.”

articles.title: Public monitoring alerts now have direct links
articles.summary: In your enterprise’s Public monitoring view, click an alert number to open the alert. You can use its URL to bookmark the finding or share it with teammates who have access.

articles.title: Polo is a Wayland compositor for the MATE desktop
articles.summary: Polo is a new Wayland compositor for MATE modelled on the desktop’s existing X11-based window manager Marco (which was forked from GNOME’s Metacity a long time ago).

articles.title: Running Android apps on Ubuntu is now surprisingly easy
articles.summary: Ubuntu doesn’t run Android apps and games natively, but Waydroid is an open-source effort that lets you use them – and it’s really easy to setup on Ubuntu.

articles.title: Firefox’s free built-in VPN removes its data limit (until next year)
articles.summary: Mozilla has lifted its 50GB data cap on Firefox’s built-in VPN until 31 January 2027. From 10 November, you can enable the free VPN in Firefox and browse as much as you like, for as long as you like, without needing to worry about reaching the fixed monthly limit.

articles.title: Khronos To Explore New High Level API For Remote Offloading
articles.summary: The Khronos Group, the industry consortium responsible for OpenGL, OpenCL, Vulkan, and other industry standard APIs has formed an exploratory group to evaluate the possibility of a high-level remote offloading API.
